# Retrieving rationale sentences within a known cited abstract

Given a claim and its cited SciFact abstract, can lexical evidence from the two neighboring sentences improve ranking of the annotated rationale? On 180 development claim–document pairs the smallest candidate weight (.25) ranked first. On 358 different evaluation pairs across 235 source documents, the weighted ranker gave mean reciprocal rank .65764, versus .66964 for scoring the center sentence alone and .67025 for BM25. The paired difference against the center-only ablation was −.01200 (document-cluster 95% interval −.02328 to −.00206). Recall at three was .6250, .6416 and .6484 respectively.

All pairs come from the official training release. The hash-based document split and exclusion of mixed claims from selection prevent claim and document overlap. The evaluation supplies the cited document in advance. Its endpoint is the rank of any annotated evidence sentence within that abstract. It does not score the verification of historical claims, stance prediction, or the recovery of every complete multi-sentence rationale. Resampling sources conditions on the selected weight and may omit dependence between claims citing several sources. [SciFact](https://aclanthology.org/2020.emnlp-main.609/) · [Design](protocol.md) · [Results](metrics.json)

Download the pinned archive to the location in the [parent instructions](../README.md). From the repository root run `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python research_v4_2/external/archival_retrieval/evidence_sentences/evaluate.py`. The script verifies the archive and regenerates the two saved outputs. Only the corpus and official training claims are opened.
